body:
I would love review from @dslomov and @ajklein. @heycam might also want to take a look since this removes any IDL annotations for transferable objects, relying on prose instead.

Some xref'ing to ECMAScript might be broken/missing still. Would love to land #638 first since it puts down some more infrastructure for that.

Summary of changes:
- Turn StructuredClone into an abstract operation that builds directly upon ECMAScript and takes a new _targetRealm_ argument so objects are actually created in a place.
- Move transfering into the StructuredClone abstract operation rather than as a special case in two different `postMessage()` algorithms.
- Define a [[Clone]] internal method, [[Detached]] internal slot, and [[Transfer]] internal method for IDL-defined objects so they can participate in the fun.
- Update all ECMAScript references to be ES6+-compatible.

I haven't used the new internal methods/slots for ECMAScript objects per @domenic's feedback. The preference was to have one giant monkey patch over lots of small ones (he worded this differently, see #697 ).
Hmm, this diff is unfortunate. Maybe it would be better with one commit that moves stuff around, then another that rewrites the structured clone section?

Overall this looks great to me. I am not sure I am in position to give a deep review (especially since I do not follow HTML5 spec travails closely), but happy to see this more rigorous approach to structured clone spec making its way into HTML5 spec.

Open issues afaict:
- this' vs this's: _leaving this as this' since there's precedent_
- https://tc39.github.io/ecma262/#typedarray-create In particular we want to use "Let defaultConstructor be the intrinsic object listed in column one of Table 50 for the value of exemplar's [[TypedArrayName]] internal slot." from the abstract operation below I think. But does intrinsic mean the original value or can ECMAScript taint what objects we'll end up creating here?
- "Otherwise, if" in the StructuredClone algorithm. Currently only used where necessary. Should we use it throughout? _made it more consistent_
- Avoid using "?" when invoking abstract operations from algorithm text not written in ECMAScripty language. _done_
- Cross-reference [[Transfer]]? [[Clone]]? _done_
- Argument name for IsTransferable, use "argument" as per IsArray? _yes_
At this point the only open issue here is https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/issues/418. Shall I wait for coordination with ECMAScript or go with a homegrown solution?

Homegrown seems reasonable.

I'd really prefer this's, especially since in this case "this" is a code object and is singular. You should only do xyzs' if xyzs is plural.
http://grammar.ccc.commnet.edu/grammar/possessives.htm has no such rule and in fact mentions "Mrs. Chambers' estate." We really need a style guide.
OK. I would like our style guide to always mandate 's for possessive.
Ready for another round of review.

I believe I addressed the outstanding feedback. Below some commentary for a couple of the points.

> It seems a bit weird that Ctrl+Fing on the spec after this change for "structured clone" gives zero results. _shrug_.

Fixed.

> should be "types"

ECMAScript doesn't think so.

> Let's go with "**The _TypedArray_ Constructors** table"

Table 50 seems better since otherwise it's out-of-sync with ECMAScript.

> Is it possible to do one commit that moves stuff around and then another that changes structured clone stuff, to avoid these kind of diffs where it looks like structured clone stuff is replacing other parts of the spec?

Done, not sure it helps much.

> What do you think of "types" instead of "objects"?

The "Type" is Object so given that we use terminology from ECMAScript I think that would be confusing.

> But it seems a bit weird to say that an object is IDL-defined or JavaScript-defined, or that an object defines an internal method.

I changed that to "the JavaScript specification" and now have that cloneable objects (or transferable objects) have an internal method. So now it flows from what they are, which seems better.

> Should this be a note? I am not sure.

Yes, the memory map is just a map, the note explains why we have it.

> This is pretty vague :(. Is there a way to make it explicit?

Suggestions? It used to be vaguer still but you didn't catch it then (it just said replace).

> I don't really care because this is nice and simple but I thought I'd point out that the ES spec seems to always do "Return a new Record { ... }."

Cross-origin objects set the precedent that we return List literals directly. Seems reasonable to follow that.

> Probably want cross-links for Boolean, Number, String, Date, RegExp, Array, Map, Set, and Object.

I have not done this, but am open to do this in the future, or make it a good first issue.

> I would prefer to preserve this xref and similar ones like it. I think this PR loses some nice prose by removing the overview sentences about what cloning and transfering means.

I tried to restore it in some form.

> is this completely gone? If so that's nice and fixes a bug which I can no longer find.

Mentioned in the commit message...

> maybe since this is a non-normative note we should just rachet it down to "a detached ImageBitmap object, or an ImageData object whose data attribute value is detached"?

I did not do this. I think even non-normative notes should be correct.

> do you need to say that it is initially false?

No. We only ever check for the true value and only ever set the value to true.

> ECMAScript doesn't think so.

It's "the List specification type" or "the Record specification type" but "the List and Record specification types". Similarly "the red car" and "the blue car" but "the red and blue cars"

> Table 50 seems better since otherwise it's out-of-sync with ECMAScript.

Why? "The TypedArray Constructors" is the caption of the table. That seems likely to be more stable than the exact table numbering (as exemplified by the `#table-49` fragment).

> I did not do this. I think even non-normative notes should be correct.

Sure, but should they reference technical concepts hidden behind `<div w-nodev>`? (This is the developer-facing infobox, after all.)

ECMAScript says "The List and Record Specification Type". Could be a typo I guess.

I prefer "Table 50" because when you read %TypedArray% algorithms that's what you'll see used. I already filed an upstream bug to resolve that in some way, but until that's decided I think we should simply match the established prose.

I think we often reference to `<div w-nodev>` things from elsewhere. I believe Wattsi deals with that somehow. There's probably some cleaning up to do in general once that starts working again since I don't think we've kept careful track.
Should I rename targetRealm to outputRealm? We could also decide on that as follow up. I'm running out of things to bikeshed.
While thinking a bit about restructuring StructuredClone into ShallowClone/DeepClone subparts (or at least structuring things in a way that'd be easier going forward) I found #754.

Given https://github.com/dslomov/ecmascript-structured-clone/issues/7#issuecomment-47403135 should we add a note that while implementations will have to use marshalling, the specification does not for convenience? E.g.:

"While technically the realm invoking StructuredCloneWithTransfer or StructuredClone has no access to the target realm passed as _targetRealm_ and implementations will have to use marshalling to implement the concepts defined in this section, the algorithms below have not done so for now for convenience and brevity."
(If we do that we should also add Allen Wirfs-Brock to the acknowledg[e]ments.)

> Cloneable objects support being cloned across event loops. I.e., across document and worker boundaries, including across documents of different origins.

I'd do s/event loops. I.e., across/event loops: i.e., across/

> IDL-defined objects that are cloneable objects

This phrase, repeated several times, seems a bit awkward. "IDL-defined cloneable objects", perhaps?

> Replace placeholderResult with transferResult, such that everything holding a reference to placeholderResult, now holds a reference to transferResult.

I still really don't know what this means. Everything? Author code? Other memory outside the browser? What is the intent behind this step?

> Originally the StructuredCloneWithTransfer abstract operation was known as the "structured clone" algorithm.

This note is great. Would it be possible to sprinkle in a few `<span id="...">`s here to preserve old links? Or will Wattsi turn those into big blue links? :-/

> Table 50

I still really don't understand why we're using the table number here. It will just cause us pain since, unlike ES, we don't have tooling that auto-updates the number when we add new tables.

In other words, I think it makes sense for ES to use table numbers internally, but other specs should use table captions.

> Let inputLen be OrdinaryGetOwnProperty(input, "length").[[Value]].

This seems wrong. If I have done `const a = []; Object.defineProperty(a, "length", { get() { return 5; } })` this will segfault (there will be no `[[Value]]`). I think you just want to do `Get(input, "length")`; I would imagine that's what implementations do.

> "While technically the realm invoking StructuredCloneWithTransfer or StructuredClone has no access to the target realm passed as targetRealm and implementations will have to use marshalling to implement the concepts defined in this section, the algorithms below have not done so for now for convenience and brevity."

I don't really agree with this note. Maybe something similar, like

"In general implementations will need to use some kind of serialization and marshalling to implement the creation of objects in _targetRealm_, as _targetRealm_ could be in a different event loop and not easily accessible to the code that invokes StructuredCloneWithTransfer or StructuredClone."

> I still really don't know what this means. Everything? Author code? Other memory outside the browser? What is the intent behind this step?

First we create a map of transferable objects to placeholder objects. Then we clone. Then we transfer the transferable objects. The cloning might have created references to the placeholder objects (because they get returned from the memory map). We then need to replace the placeholder objects with the objects we ended up transferring. That's what structured clone coupled with transferring does.

> This note is great. Would it be possible to sprinkle in a few `<span id="...">`s here to preserve old links?

I preserved the old link for the main algorithm. I guess I could also add an id for the old internal algorithm, but that seems less needed now, no? Not aware of anything pointing to that.
Yeah, I guess that is probably not that important.

> I'd do s/event loops. I.e., across/event loops: i.e., across/

I prefer to leave this as-is. The length stuff turned out to be fine per IRC. Time to rebase and squash (apart from that first commit)?
The problem is that the second sentence is not a complete sentence.

Last nits:

> Let inputLen be OrdinaryGetOwnProperty(input, "length").[[Value]].

needs to become two steps so you can do `!`. I guess the temp variable would be _inputLenDesc_ or something.

> Let output be ArrayCreate(inputLen, outputProto).

needs !

LGTM otherwise, feel free to squash and merge with those fixed.
@domenic why would OrdinaryGetOwnProperty need !?

Because it returns a completion record and we need to show that it doesn't fail?

I guess ES is inconsistent about this; only one of its call sites does the explicit assert. Probably all of them should though...
It doesn't return a completion record though. It only ever returns a record or undefined, never a completion record. (I have a PR outstanding against ECMAScript to remove the existing ! usage.)

Hmm I was kind of under the impression that per https://tc39.github.io/ecma262/#sec-implicit-completion-values all abstract operations returned completion records, but OK, I guess it makes sense for this one to not do so.
Thanks (note that we have quite a bit of existing usage that does not use it either).
